  Readable gloss: "Few Hebrew words reveal as much about ancient Israelite thought as davar (דָּבָר). Appearing nearly 1,500 times, it seamlessly bridges what English splits into 'word' and 'thing' — because in Hebrew thought, a spoken word is not merely sound but a substantive reality with force and consequence. God's davar creates, commands, and judges; a prophet's davar is simultaneously a message and an event. The plural devarim can mean 'words,' 'deeds,' 'matters,' or 'chronicles,' depending on context, making this noun the backbone of biblical narrative and legal discourse alike."

    Existing Spanish translations: Palabra-de, palabra-de, palabra-de-
